🧐🤔Reflecting on this week….💙
 As a City Council representative and community leader, it has always been my intent to represent every part of District 7, while understanding that the work is always bigger than any one district.
 First and foremost, I thank God for the opportunity to serve. It is a privilege I don’t take lightly, and I’m incredibly grateful to represent such an amazing constituency.
 The pictures I’m sharing are just a few of the stories and investments happening across District 7—investments that are making our district stronger and positioning Chattanooga for an even stronger future.
 My team and I keep up with these stories, but more importantly, we keep up with the people and the conversations behind them.
 Because community work is not always easy, but it is absolutely worth it—and it is NEVER done in silos.
 And whether I’m showing up to support an initiative, sitting in another meeting, working through an idea with community, or literally taking orders at the register at Cocoa Cafe 😂☕️—I’m in the work! I believe leadership means being present, being accessible, and being willing to roll up your sleeves and serve wherever I’m needed.
 When you see the work, just know there are tons of people behind it. People who have workshopped ideas with me, attended countless meetings, asked tough questions, offered different perspectives, and yes… even told me, “That’s not a good idea.” 😂
 And I appreciate every single one of them.
 Because without my community, I wouldn’t be able to do this work for the betterment of OUR community.
 The good.
 The bad.
 The ugly.
 And the beautiful.
 All of it is part of the work. All of it matters. And all of it is part of Building Stronger Communities. 💪🏾🏙️❤️
 Cheers to continuing to do this work—together. 🥂🏾
 And yes… sometimes that means City Councilwoman by day, barista by afternoon. 😂☕️

Since Dolly’s passing, it’s been hard for all of us at the library to put into words what she meant to us.
 Today, we had the chance to pause, come together, and remember her as a community.
 Thank you to everyone who stopped by to share a memory, write a message, or simply spend a moment with us. It meant a lot to see so many people come together for Dolly.
 And a special thank you to Chattanooga PLF for hosting a Free book drive in Dolly’s honor. Dolly spent so much of her life putting books into the hands of children, and giving away books felt like the perfect way to honor her.
 Free books for children. That’s what Dolly wanted, and that’s what the Foundation delivered.

items.content_text:
River City Company's Emerging Producers: Where are they now?
 Pedro Abriles, a 2024 Emerging Producers program graduate, has kept busy between community work, composing and producing music, and sound production for a variety of events. Pedro's most recent project involves the transformation of a well-known Chattanooga landmark: the vacant Parkway Towers building beside Highway 27, known for decades as simply "the Junk Building" for its graffitied rooftop billboard that now reads "Love."
 The new "Love" mural is the result of a partnership between Pedro and singer-songwriter, Steve Derthick, whose third album Pedro was producing. Pedro was motivated to find a way to change the old billboard from "Junk" to a more positive message for people driving through the city. "What if instead of junk, the billboard said something hopeful, like love?" The two had just finished recording Derthick's newest song, "City of Love."
 When Pedro was able to secure permission from the owners of Parkway Towers, he enlisted the help of local artist and creative strategist Rondell Crier for the planning of the mural and an accompanying creative engagement experience that allowed the community to contribute to the artwork. Volunteers from Noah's Painting completed the mural, and members of the community were invited to paint 36 wooden hearts in memory of loved ones that would later be installed on the billboard.
 The project was filmed by cinematographer Christian Eaves to be featured in the music video for Steve Derthick's song, "City of Love." We are incredibly proud of Pedro for facilitating such an impactful project, and we look forward to following his future work! 
 Watch the music video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SeORVaCHMq0

 In some jurisdictions, fewer than half of households read to their five-year-olds more than three times a week.

items.title: Captain Paul Maupin Retires After 21 Years of Service with the HCSO Hamilton County, TN
items.content_text:
Captain Paul Maupin Retires After 21 Years of Service with the HCSO
 Hamilton County, TN – Today, Sheriff Austin Garrett, Chief Deputy Spencer Daniels, and members of the Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office recognized Captain Paul Maupin's retirement.
 Captain Maupin began his career with the HCSO in 2006 and has dedicated the last two decades to serving the citizens of Hamilton County. Throughout his career, he has served in numerous assignments and leadership positions across the agency's various units. His service included assignments with SWAT, as a Field Training Officer (FTO), a member of the HCSO Honor Guard, and the Dignitary Protection Unit, among others.
 Paul earned an Associate of Science degree in Criminal Justice, a Bachelor of Science degree in Public Administration, and completed the Southeast Law Enforcement Command Academy (SECLA) hosted by the University of Tennessee. Paul served as a Staff Sergeant in the United States Marine Corps from 2001 to 2009, serving in both the active-duty and Reserve components.
 “Goodbyes are never easy, and Captain Maupin’s retirement will leave a significant void in our ranks. His years of service to this agency and the citizens of Hamilton County have made a tremendous impact, and he has played an integral part through his leadership and sacrifice, helping the HCSO become an agency that is “leading the way.”  We wish him all the best in his retirement and in all future endeavors,” stated Sheriff Austin Garrett.
 As he begins this next chapter, the Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office extends its appreciation to Captain Maupin for his 21 years of dedicated service. We congratulate Captain Maupin on his retirement and wish him and his family all the best in the future.

 Today, the once-vacant storefront is a welcoming neighborhood destination—and River Street is home to some of the best crepes in town. 
 That’s the goal of Scenic Storefronts: helping businesses invest in their buildings, activate commercial spaces, and create places that add energy and character to our neighborhoods. Thank you to the City of Chattanooga for supporting this program.

This week, community leaders, educators, youth-serving organizations, and partners from across Chattanooga-Hamilton County came together for the Chattanooga-Hamilton County Adolescent Development Learning Series to explore that question and build a shared understanding of adolescent development.

The two-day gathering also marked the launch of Chattanooga 2.0’s newest Big Bet: Thriving Adolescence—a long-term community commitment to creating the conditions young people need to develop, explore their interests, build strong relationships, and pursue their futures.

There is no single organization that can create those conditions alone. It will take all of us working together, and listening to young people themselves, to build a community where more adolescents can find meaningful experiences, strong relationships, and clear pathways toward their futures.

We’re grateful to everyone who joined us and helped begin this next chapter! https://lnkd.in/ghrUMYMY

G20 trade accelerated in the second quarter of 2026, boosted primarily by merchandise imports and services trade.
 Measured in current US dollars, quarter-on-quarter import growth rose markedly to 6.7%, from the 5.2% growth recorded in the previous quarter, reflecting strong increases in a number of G20 economies.
 G20 merchandise exports growth remained broadly flat at 5.9%.
 Preliminary estimates also point to an acceleration in services trade, with exports rising by 3.4% and imports by 2.5%, as compared to 2.0% and 1.5% respectively in Q1 2026.

 As part of the annual City as Text activity, students explored neighborhoods across Chattanooga, taking in the history, local businesses, public spaces, transportation and more before returning to campus to share what they discovered.
 Lifelong Chattanoogan and community advocate Krue Brock joined the discussion, encouraging students to stay curious, seek out opportunities to learn and get involved in their new community.
 “You’re one relationship away from solving a lot of things that could be better,” Brock told students.
 Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/incoming-utc-honors-college-student…/

items.content_text:
UPDATE: We've received several questions about our recent post regarding The Field. We intentionally did not identify the exact location because this is a sensitive and sacred historic site, and there is still important work ahead to protect, preserve, and honor those buried there.
 The Field is a historic potter's field containing hundreds of unmarked graves, many of whom have long been forgotten in the historical record. Trust for Public Land, local partners, and community members have been working to research, protect, and tell the story of this important site. 
 The City's recent acquisition of the remaining portions of The Field ensures its long-term protection and represents a major milestone in this ongoing effort.
 We would also like to recognize Red Bank resident and artist Megan Ledbetter, whose work has helped bring additional awareness to the history and significance of The Field. Learn more about her project here: https://www.meganledbetter.com/portfolio-2/the-field
 For more information about The Field and the ongoing work being led by Trust for Public Land, please visit: https://www.tpl.org/our-work/the-field
 Thank you for your interest and support as we continue this important work.
Over the past two years, the City of Red Bank has worked alongside Trust for Public Land (TPL) and the Hill Pointe HOA to secure ownership of all remaining portions of The Field. Today, we are excited to celebrate a major milestone as the City officially acquires 100% of this property through the generous land donation from the Hill Pointe HOA.
 This acquisition ensures the long-term protection of this sensitive and historically significant site while allowing the City to move into the next phase of thoughtfully honoring and preserving its legacy. While this work will take time, today's closing represents an important step forward.
 We extend our sincere thanks to the Hill Pointe HOA and its residents for their generosity and partnership. We are especially grateful to Daniela Peterson and the entire team at Trust for Public Land, whose dedication and persistence were instrumental in making this vision a reality. We also want to thank City Attorney Arnold Stulce and City staff who helped navigate this multi-year effort from concept to completion.
 This is a significant accomplishment for our community, and we look forward to sharing more as we continue the important work of protecting and honoring The Field for future generations.

items.content_text:
Chattanooga has lost a remarkable visionary and devoted champion of our community with the passing of Shane Morrow. Our prayers are with his family, friends, and all who were touched by his life and leadership. As we mourn together, we also celebrate his extraordinary life and the lasting inspiration he brought to so many through his impactful work.
Chattanooga Business Elite joins our community in mourning the passing of Shane Morrow—a true legend, visionary, cultural leader, artist, advocate, and champion for Chattanooga.
 Shane dedicated his life to creating opportunities and opening doors for others, especially Black artists, creatives, and young people. Through his leadership with RISE Chattanooga, formerly Jazzanooga, he created spaces where music, art, culture, and community could come together. He understood that the arts were more than entertainment—they could heal, educate, empower, connect, and transform an entire community.
 We were honored to recognize Shane as a past CBE Homage Award recipient. That recognition represented only a small reflection of the enormous impact he made throughout our city. His legacy lives in every artist he encouraged, every young person he inspired, every neighborhood he invested in, and every cultural space he helped create.
 Shane did not simply participate in Chattanooga’s cultural movement—he helped shape it. His presence, passion, vision, and commitment to our community will never be forgotten.
 On behalf of Chattanooga Business Elite, we extend our deepest condolences, prayers, and love to his partner James, his family, friends, colleagues, loved ones, and the entire RISE Chattanooga community.
 Rest well, Shane. Thank you for giving so much of yourself to Chattanooga. Your work mattered, your life made a difference, and your legacy will continue to rise through us all. 🕊️

 Hamilton County, TN – On August 27, 2026, HCSO personnel took Robert Corey Ripple into custody in Meigs County after a months-long effort to locate and apprehend him.
 Ripple has an extensive criminal history, and warrants for his arrest were first issued in June 2026 for charges of trespassing and theft of property. Ripple repeatedly fled law enforcement, resulting in additional warrants being issued.
 Ripple currently faces the following charges: 
 • Evading Arrest x3
 • Theft of Property
 • Criminal Trespassing x2
 • Off-Road Motor Vehicle on Highway
 This arrest was the result of extensive investigative work and the combined efforts of the HCSO Criminal Warrants Unit, the HCSO NSI, the HCSO K-9 Unit, and the Meigs County Sheriff’s Office. We want to thank the Meigs County Sheriff’s Office for their assistance in this. 
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.content_text:
ArtsBuild’s Board and staff stand with ArtsBuild’s President and his family as they navigate the heartbreaking loss of the much-beloved, Shane Morrow.
 We encourage our community to read the post from RISE Chattanooga for more information. At this time, the family has asked for privacy and space as they walk through the next steps. We are holding James, his family, and all those who loved Shane in our hearts.
 If our community needs anything during this time, please reach out to our main telephone number, 4two3-756-278seven.
It is with profound sadness that we share the passing of Shane Morrow, visionary and founder of RISE Chattanooga.
 There really are no words big enough for this loss.
 Shane believed deeply in the power of creativity, culture and community to change lives. What began with Jazzanooga grew under his vision into RISE Chattanooga — Responsive Initiatives for Social Empowerment — because Shane understood that the work was always bigger than music.
 It was about people.
 It was about creating opportunities where they did not exist. Making room for voices that had too often been overlooked. Investing in Black artists, creatives and entrepreneurs. Preserving our stories and celebrating our culture. Building community. Pouring into East Chattanooga. And using art and creativity as tools for empowerment, economic opportunity and real transformation.
 Shane didn’t just talk about what Chattanooga could be. He created spaces, programs and opportunities that helped move us toward it.
 Today, we grieve our founder, our leader, our friend and the visionary who challenged us to think bigger about what was possible for our communities.
 Our hearts are with Shane’s family and loved ones, and with everyone who had the privilege of knowing him, working alongside him, learning from him or simply experiencing something that existed because Shane had the audacity to imagine it.
 RISE was Shane’s vision, but his greatest gift was making that vision big enough for an entire community to see itself in it.
 During this incredibly difficult time, Shane’s family asks that their privacy be respected as they grieve and navigate this tremendous loss. We ask our community to honor that request and surround them with love from a respectful distance.
 For those asking how they can show their love and support for Shane’s family, please visit the link below:
 https://www.supportnow.org/the-family-of-shane-morrow…
 Rest well, Shane.
 Thank you for the vision.
 Thank you for the work.
 Thank you for the opportunities.
 Thank you for believing in our community.
 We will continue to RISE.
 #TogetherWeRISE

Every night of a two-week trip to Chile, students Adam Williams and Samuel Jayroe would look up at a sky so dark they could see the Milky Way. 🌌
 Along with a group of UTC students and faculty researchers, they stayed in a remote astrocamp tucked away in Chile’s countryside.
 During the day, they hiked among shrubs and rocky hills as they collected environmental data that could help researchers better understand the degu—one of Chile’s most recognizable native animals.
 The students joined Dr. Loren Hayes' two-decade study of Chile's native degus, where Dr. Azad Hossain's geospatial research is helping uncover how changing landscapes influence where the animals live.
 Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/utc-students-take-geospatial-resear…/

NORTH RIVER ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
 SECOND MAJOR GROUNDBREAKING UNDER COUNTYWIDE SCHOOL FACILITIES IMPROVEMENT PLAN. 
 Dr. Justin Robertson says this is one of the most complicated projects Hamilton County Schools has taken on — but in two years, students will be learning inside this brand-new building.
 WHAT THIS MEANS FOR KIDS: The goal is to create an incredible experience for students and families while maintaining high academic expectations and introducing new opportunities through a partnership with the YMCA, a first for Hamilton County Schools.
 For example, about 800 students will be able to take free swimming lessons, helping teach an important life skill and promote water safety.
 Chairman Ken Smith says District 3 is known for making major investments in education, pointing to the new turf field at Hixson High School as one example.
 He says projects like this don’t happen without collaboration.
 The new school will combine a state-of-the-art learning environment with community support from the YMCA…. creating new opportunities for the students who attend.

items.content_text:
Today we're sharing another look at CPD's newly launched Drone First Responder (DFR) pilot program. In case you missed it, our DFR pilot program includes two prepositioned drones located at CFD Fire Stations 4 & 9. When needed, officers in our Real Time Intelligence Center (RTIC) can launch these drones and stream live footage to the operators and responding officers. 
 Why DFR?
 1. The drones can arrive quickly and provide first responders with intel to make faster, more informed decisions.
 2. They can help improve resource deployment.
 3. Perhaps most importantly, they can enhance the safety of first responders and the public.
 Other things to know about DFR
 1. These drones are NOT used for routine patrol or surveillance.
 2. This pilot program was fully funded by grant money.
 3. You can see details about every flight, including maps, duration, and call types at the DFR dashboard on https://hubs.la/Q04vqVRj0.

Over the past two years, the City of Red Bank has worked alongside Trust for Public Land (TPL) and the Hill Pointe HOA to secure ownership of all remaining portions of The Field. Today, we are excited to celebrate a major milestone as the City officially acquires 100% of this property through the generous land donation from the Hill Pointe HOA.
 This acquisition ensures the long-term protection of this sensitive and historically significant site while allowing the City to move into the next phase of thoughtfully honoring and preserving its legacy. While this work will take time, today's closing represents an important step forward.
 We extend our sincere thanks to the Hill Pointe HOA and its residents for their generosity and partnership. We are especially grateful to Daniela Peterson and the entire team at Trust for Public Land, whose dedication and persistence were instrumental in making this vision a reality. We also want to thank City Attorney Arnold Stulce and City staff who helped navigate this multi-year effort from concept to completion.
 This is a significant accomplishment for our community, and we look forward to sharing more as we continue the important work of protecting and honoring The Field for future generations.
